name: Ling-3.0-flash

sources.note: aggregator mirror of the Artificial Analysis Coding Index, read 2026-11-19; no per-row dates; upstream AA pages not reachable

purpose: inclusionAI states: a next-generation native hybrid reasoning model for real-world productivity workflows (coding, general and deep-research agents), trained in 10,000+ interactive environments, matching or beating the 1T-class Ring-2.6-1T with 12 % of its parameters.

lineage.how_derived: native hybrid linear attention from the start of pre-training (not converted)

license.name: MIT (card tag; no LICENSE file in the repository)
license.notes: Card YAML says mit for both the model and the official GGUF repository; neither has a LICENSE file, the text could not be read.

architecture.gguf_arch: bailing hybrid (name not verified; llama.cpp support needs a turboquant build or PR 26608 per HF discussion 4)
architecture.attention: 35 Kimi Delta Attention layers and 7 gated MLA layers (5:1), 2 dense layers
architecture.why_this_design: inclusionAI states: native hybrid linear attention (5:1 KDA to MLA, fine-grained diagonal gating, 1/64 sparse MoE) gives long-context efficiency and low compute per token; training schedule 8K, 32K, 256K.

pc-12gb.notes: estimate from the file size (77.0 GB) against the budget of docs/hardware: 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM = 60 GB; about 12% of the file can sit in VRAM, the rest streams from RAM (decode speed depends on that); no smaller official quant; a community 3-bit class file would be about 60 GB (HF discussion 14 reports a Q3_K_M of 62.7 GiB)

engine_support.notes: Official GGUFs exist, but mainline llama.cpp did not load the model on 2026-08-04 to 08-07; users needed a turboquant build or a PR (HF discussion 4). Tona would need a new module (KDA layers, gated MLA).

benchmarks.variant: API / full precision, not a quant

benchmarks.name: AA Intelligence Index
benchmarks.harness: from a search result snippet; GLM-5.3 (max) scored 60 on the same page; page not fetched

strengths: 5.1 B active parameters: fast; users pair it with an agent harness and call it underrated
KDA layers keep the KV small
weaknesses: Independent Coding Index 50.6 against 73.0 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and 68.1 (Qwen3.8-27B) on the same mirror
Chat template problems with multi-argument tool calls (HF discussion 4, 10)
Vendor benchmark values are in chart images, not readable as text
soft.behavior: Thinking on by default (enable_thinking false to disable); recommended temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20.
best_for: fast agent workers on 32 GB VRAM + 128 GB RAM or 24 GB + 96 GB machines
avoid_for: 16 GB VRAM + 64 GB RAM machines at the official quants
soft.maturity: inclusionAI: Ling / Ring family since 2025, 2.6 predecessor; main repo 8k downloads, 19 discussions.

user_reports.summary: "Totally underrated" when paired with an agent harness, feels better because it is fast
Own GGUFs without imatrix: Q4_K_M with Q8_0 attention is +0.73 % perplexity against F16 (4.3849 against 4.3532): takes quantization well
llama.cpp did not run it at release; needed a fork or PR and a modified Jinja template for multi-argument tool calls

tona_fit.reason: MIT by card and a real fit for 24 to 32 GB VRAM classes, but the only independent coding number (50.6) is clearly below the Qwen3.8 family that Tona already runs, and its smallest official quant (77 GB) does not reach the 16 GB + 64 GB class. Revisit if a 3-bit quant with measured quality appears.
blockers: Tona has no KDA/MLA module (engine support, not a quality judgement)
